articles.title: Tata Motors raises Iveco takeover offer price to 14.40 euro per share
No higher bid: Tata Motors’ final price faces crucial test as Iveco shareholders hold the key
Stellantis and Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles broaden partnership to develop vehicles in Pune
Tata Motors, Stellantis expand partnership: New deal details explained
Tata Motors sweetens Iveco offer as key investors hold out

article_briefs.brief: Tata Motors lifted its all‑cash tender offer for Iveco to €14.40 per share, raising the implied transaction value to €3.91 billion if all 271.2 million shares are tendered. The premium is 33.47 % to the 17 July 2025 price and 6.77 % to the 29 July 2025 price. Funding for the extra payout will come from an €85 million credit facility with MUFG Bank.

The €3.91‑billion bid for Iveco is now in its final phase with a “best and final” offer of €14.40 per share. Exor has committed its 27.06 % stake (43 % voting rights) while other large shareholders holding about 20 % may decide if the 80 % acceptance threshold can be met. If completed, the combined entity would generate roughly €21 billion of annual revenue and sell about 5,90,000 vehicles.

Stellantis India, Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Ltd and its subsidiary signed a definitive agreement expanding their partnership into advanced vehicle technology and product collaboration. Tata will provide vehicle architecture and technology, while Stellantis will use its engineering capabilities to develop models for more than 50 global markets, with production at the FIAPL 50:50 joint venture in Pune.

Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles and Stellantis have formalised an expanded partnership that merges Tata’s vehicle architecture with Stellantis’s global product‑development expertise. The deal targets vehicle development for over 50 markets and manufacturing in India at the FIAPL joint venture, leveraging Stellantis’s portfolio of 14 brands and worldwide presence.

Tata Motors raised its offer for Iveco to €14.40 per share, its “best and final” price, after activist Petrus Advisers rejected the earlier bid. Acceptance stands at 28.4 % of shares; three investors (Davidson Kempner, Syquant Capital, Petrus Advisers) hold about 20.4 % and have not tendered. Exor holds 27.06 % (43 % voting rights). The revised price represents a 6.77 % premium to the 29 July 2025 closing price.

key_points.text: Tata Motors increased its all‑cash offer for Iveco to €14.40 per share, raising the implied transaction value to €3.91 billion if all 271.2 million shares are tendered, and added an €85 million credit facility to fund the extra payout.
The revised offer represents a 33.47 % premium to Iveco’s share price on 17 July 2025 and a 6.77 % premium to the price on 29 July 2025.
Tata Motors declared the €14.40 per share price as “best and final” with no further increases planned.

Exor, Iveco’s largest shareholder, has committed its 27.06 % stake (43 % of voting rights) supporting the deal, while three other major investors (Davidson Kempner, Syquant Capital, Petrus Advisers) together hold about 20 % (20.4 %) and have not tendered, leaving acceptance at only 28.4 % of shares.
Completion of the acquisition would create a global commercial‑vehicle group with roughly €21 billion of annual revenue and about 5,90,000 vehicles sold per year.

Tata Motors is expanding its partnership with Stellantis: the companies signed a definitive agreement to combine Tata’s vehicle architecture and technology with Stellantis’s global product‑development expertise, targeting vehicle development for more than 50 markets and manufacturing in India at the FIAPL joint venture.

industry_context.text: The expanded Tata‑Stellantis collaboration aims to leverage India’s engineering and manufacturing capacity to develop vehicles for international markets, reflecting a broader trend of Indian OEMs partnering with global firms to boost export potential.

Stellantis’s portfolio of 14 automotive brands and its worldwide footprint (Europe, North America, South America, Middle East, Africa, Asia‑Pacific) could provide Tata Motors access to diversified market channels, influencing competitive dynamics in the commercial‑vehicle sector.
